key_insight: Single-qubit re-uploading circuits can match the expressivity of multi-qubit circuits with the same encoding budget, but they are much harder to train in first-order optimization because their state evolution is phase-locked to fewer tangent directions.
engineering_relevance: For quantum ML workflow design, this means choosing a narrower serial circuit may save qubits without losing function class, but it can significantly reduce optimization reliability and increase training cost.
method: Analyzes angle-encoded variational circuits as truncated Fourier series for 1D inputs.
Proves tangent-direction limits for serial circuits and compares them to multi-qubit control circuits at equal encoding budget.
Benchmarks gradient descent, Adam, and Levenberg–Marquardt on exact flat-spectrum targets and real-world time-series tasks.
evidence_signal: Across 100 runs, the serial circuit showed far lower optimization success than the control: at E=32 it converged in 3/53/83 runs versus 99/100/100, and on real data the control reached the optimum in at least 98 runs while the serial model often lagged and sometimes had up to about 1.5× higher test error.
watch_item: The results are specific to 1D angle-encoded re-uploading circuits and fixed step-budget first-order training, so the optimization gap may differ for other encodings, architectures, or higher-dimensional inputs.
paper_title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
